longForm.overview:
🇯🇲 is the emoji of green-and-gold coded national-identity read — the green-and-gold banner, the saltire-cross coded flex, and the universal 'green-and-gold pulse' tag for Jamaica pride. Where 🇺🇳 reads as neutral-coded diplomacy read and 🏳️‍🌈 reads as rainbow-coded pride read, 🇯🇲 captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate green-and-gold coded identity — a 'green-and-gold 🇯🇲' heritage check-in or a 'saltire-cross pulse 🇯🇲' Reggae-Boyz reveal. The green-and-gold banner cue borrows from Jamaica's national flag tradition and the modern heritage-coded aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as green-and-gold coded rather than literal travel-coded flag.

In real-world usage 🇯🇲 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate green-and-gold energy. A partner sends it on a 'green-and-gold 🇯🇲' heritage check-in. A friend sends it on a 'saltire-cross pulse 🇯🇲' pride reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'green-and-gold coded 🇯🇲' heritage-month thread. The green-and-gold banner cue is what makes the emoji feel green-and-gold coded — it is not just 'flag,' it is 'green-and-gold coded Jamaica-pride moment.'

What separates 🇯🇲 from the rest of the flag family is the green-and-gold register. The emoji is not saying 'rainbow pride' (🏳️‍🌈), 'black rebellion' (🏴), or 'checkered finish' (🏁). It is saying 'green-and-gold coded Jamaica-coded identity,' which carries a specific national-flag tradition. That is why 🇯🇲 travels especially well on partner heritage check-ins, Reggae-Boyz reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with green-and-gold energy.
